newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokeswoman Sophie Petzell said Commissioner Anita Gradin would meet leading non-governmental organisations active in the fight against trafficking and sexual abuse of children on Friday. She said the hearing would take place at the Centre Borschette in Brussels and that journalists were invited to attend the meeting and the buffet-lunch.

Spokesman Peter Guilford said Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan had met Norvegian Foreign Affairs Minister Bjoern Tore Godal and Fisheries Minister Karl Eirik Schuett-Pedersen in the morning to discuss the Commission proposal to impose an anti-dumping duty on Norwegian salmon imports. He said a decision on this issue, which would be neither political nor influenced by the forthcoming UK elections, was expected in the next few weeks.

Guilford said there was a convergence of views between the Norwegian Ministers and Sir Leon Brittan on the fact that the European Economic Area allows for measures to be taken in areas where the EU "acquis communautaire" has not been integrated. Fisheries is one of those areas, he said.

Asked to react to the Israeli rejection of the Commission proposal for of a code of conduct, spokesman Josep Coll i Carbo said the Commission's role was to help but that willingness should be shown on all sides.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/273: Commission hearing with NGOs on fighting trafficking and sexual exploitation of children - Friday 11 April Borschette Brussels.
- IP/97/275: Commission supports industrial restructuring in Zuid-Limburg (NL).
- IP/97/276: Commission supports industrial restructuring in Limburg and Turnhout (B).
- IP/97/277: Commission supports industrial restructuring in Burgundy.
- IP/97/278: Commission supports reconversion in 8 Italian regions in industrial decline.
- IP/97/279: ECU 174.5 million for industrial areas in the United Kingdom.
- IP/97/281: Commission launches an ambitious programme to promote road safety in the Union.
- IP/97/282: French textile plan: Commission refuses to authorize past aid but is willing to discuss a general reduction in employers' social security contributions.
- IP/97/283: Through the fifth framework programme, the Commission proposes new European research policy.
- Commission Green Paper on relations between the European Union and the ACP countries on the eve of the 21st century - Challenges and option for a new partnership.
- European Commission - Towards ther 5th framework programme.
